prompts:
Use case: ui-mockup / stylized-concept. Create ONE polished art-direction sheet for Bottle Harmony, square 2048x2048, using the supplied approved sheet as a STYLE REFERENCE, not an edit target. Preserve the established straight-on CLASSIC GLASS BOTTLE silhouette, thin cool cyan-gray glass rims, restrained highlights, dark charcoal-blue background and luminous jade/coral/yellow liquids. This is feasible stylized mobile puzzle art, not realistic photography or ornate fantasy illustration.

Title "三种机关外观 · 视觉效果稿". Small subtitle "柔光布盖 / 深色薄木匣 / 百叶护笼". A clean aligned 3 by 3 matrix of bottle details with generous negative space. ROWS are the three material families. COLUMNS are states; exact headers "初次锁定", "展开示意", "已见重锁". At left of rows, small family names "柔光布盖", "深色薄木匣", "百叶护笼". Small footer "展开结束后仅保留原玻璃 · 已见液体不再遮盖". No phone UI, no game toolbar, no coins, treasure, reward, numbers of levels, arrows, new interaction buttons or decorative cards.

Scale and geometry: all nine underlying bottles have exactly the same reference classic-glass dimensions. Covers fit snugly within a narrow bottle slot, maximum 10% wider than glass body; no flared skirts, wide doors across neighboring cells, bulky crates or cages, no reduction of glass size. Glass cavity proportions remain as in reference; never fill a neck or glass stem. All revealed states show the SAME liquid stack, top to bottom one portion jade, two portions coral and one portion yellow. Preserve these exact relative liquid quantities across all visible states, no new liquid created. The first column hides contents COMPLETELY: opaque cloth/wood/slats with absolutely no visible liquid or color hints through cracks.

Row 1 CLOTH:
First column: opaque slate-blue-gray matte-satin woven cloth, rounded covered mouth, narrow neck, softly fitted shoulders, just 3-5 large vertical folds, close narrow curved hem at glass base. Subtle weave only on close view. Small sewn JADE condition patch at front center, white circle symbol and exactly FOUR tiny white dots. No exposed bottle opening.
Middle column: a single held instant of cloth being lifted upward as a coherent soft cap with gentle folding. The same glass bottle's lower and middle liquid are visible beneath the rising hem; fabric remains a narrow folded silhouette above upper glass. Clearly an opening transition, not a static accessory left behind. No hands or pulling ropes.
Third column: fully visible original glass and complete liquid stack. No opaque cloth at all. A VERY SMALL champagne-gold mechanical latch attached to a shallow anchored base secures the glass at the lower side and communicates cannot lift/tilt; do not cover the liquid with a belt or wide padlock.

Row 2 WOOD:
First column: a slim deep walnut-brown protective CASE shaped with softly squared sides, beveled corners, a narrowed upper shoulder, fine vertical wood grain, one precise front opening seam. Cool shadow, warm subtle edges, little champagne-gold latch, no oversized rivets. Fully opaque. A small same-size jade four-dot condition plate on the front, matching row 1's information. Not a treasure chest and not a large rectangular shipping crate.
Middle column: FRONT PANELS OPEN ONLY SLIGHTLY (20-25 degrees) as a single opening pose, within a narrow silhouette, showing the SAME reference glass and jade/coral/yellow liquid stack inside. Keep slim hinges and refined dark wood edges. No wide door wings obscuring neighboring cells.
Third column: fully exposed glass, no opaque wooden walls blocking known liquid. At most a minimal open side frame and shallow base, with a tiny latched retainer showing relocked. Preserve clear readability of every liquid portion. No persistent wide open doors.

Row 3 CAGE:
First column: a fitted elegant dark blue-gray metal protective cage with 4-5 fine champagne-gray structural uprights and a compact top frame. OPAQUE horizontal blue-gray shutter slats completely close every viewing area, including front AND sides, so no liquid is visible anywhere. Looks like a compact protective cabinet with louver shutters, not an animal cage or prison. Tiny champagne-gold door latch. Small same-size jade four-dot condition badge on front.
Middle column: shutter slats fold or retract upward INSIDE the fitted frame, revealing the SAME reference glass bottle and same liquid. A narrow gate is just beginning to release; avoid large swung-out door shapes. This is a transition instant.
Third column: shutter slats have completely retracted, leaving ONLY a few slim vertical uprights and a small visibly closed gate latch at the side, so all previously known liquid colors remain clearly visible. No opaque panel over glass and no bars thick enough to hide liquid. The cage is anchored to its small base.

Common language: identical warm champagne-gold accents and condition badge scale, restrained rim lighting, quiet contact shadows. These are three surface treatments for the same existing rules, not different game modes. FOUR dots always represent the four-portion condition and are not a progress bar. Gold latch is a restrained sign of locked access; no large keyholes that imply an additional key is required for these color-condition examples. The artwork should look comfortable and refined on a dark phone board; material detail secondary to liquid color. Ensure all Chinese labels are legible and exact, no extra explanatory paragraphs or English gibberish. This is a concept review sheet, not a pixel-accurate shipped screenshot.

Precisely refine the supplied Bottle Harmony 3x3 visual concept sheet; keep all Chinese text, layout, three material families, palette, lighting, glass style and state meanings unchanged.
Correct these details only:
1. Every JADE circular condition badge must show the white circle plus EXACTLY FOUR small white dots in a neat centered row, not five. Check badges in both cloth states, both wood states and the closed cage state. Do not turn them into counters.
2. In the WOOD MIDDLE cell (opening pose), the revealed GLASS BOTTLE must have the same width AND height as the WOOD RIGHT cell and CLOTH RIGHT cell reference bottle. Keep the glass neck/mouth at the same row-relative height and base at the same row-relative height. Do NOT shrink the glass to fit the box. Make the walnut panels visibly thin, door angle shallow and case close fitting around the full-size glass. Outer frame can be narrowly wider, never bulky.
3. Refine wood case silhouettes to have softly ROUNDED shoulders and beveled edges, matching a protective bottle case. Remove the harsh coffin-like polygon shoulders. Slightly quieter wood grain and narrow champagne-gold latch, warm refined walnut material.
4. Across all nine cells use uniform underlying glass bottle proportions and a cover footprint no more than around ten percent wider. Avoid resizing glass between closed/open/relatched states. Keep already known liquids fully readable in the entire right column.
Everything else stays as in the supplied image. No new labels, no actions, no permanent opaque covers in relocked states.
constraints: Preserve approved glass, bottle size, six-column layout, pour timing and player data in implementation.
Opening column illustrates an intermediate pose; completed opening removes the enclosure.
Known colors remain visible after undo relocks access.
Three single-bottle families approved as first-version visual baseline; exact geometry, board adaptation and device acceptance remain implementation work.
